title: People’s Mañanera October 28
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**24.70 billion pesos for water in Guadalajara, without debt or privatization  
** “We do not agree with the private operation of the water system,” President
Claudia Sheinbaum declared. The 24.70 billion peso (US$1.32 billion)
investment will improve water supply for 30 years, without raising rates and
avoiding the need to commit up to 56 billion pesos (US$3 billion) from
Jalisco.

**Mexican Government Calls for Audit of More Than 20 Years of INE Contracts  
** “We are going to put an end to electoral ‘coyotes.’” The President proposed
strengthening Talleres Gráficos, ensuring contract transparency and penalizing
irregularities. Sheinbaum indicated that in relation to the changes in the
Federal Electoral Institute (INE), “the 2027 elections are not in question.”

**Sheinbaum to Le Pen: Mexico brings honesty, solidarity, and fraternity to
the table  
** “She is misinformed,” replied the President, in response to comments by far
right French leader Marine Le Pen. Sheinbaum said that “the ‘Mexicanization’
that should reach the whole world is that of the values of the Mexican
people.”

**Lie Detector**

  * It is not true that Guadalupe Taddei was appointed president of the INE by Morena
  * It is not true that IMSS Modality 40 was suspended or eliminated because the government ran out of money
  * It is not true that IMSS doctors earn 10,000 pesos (US$535) a month and that Cuban doctors in Mexico earn more than their Mexican counterparts
  * It is not true that mammogram coverage in Mexico “is minimal and insufficient”
  * It is not true that the amendments to the Federal Criminal Code and the Federal Law on the Protection of Industrial Property “are a step toward censorship”
